results: A shared norm comparison bounds the difference of two actual fixed points using contraction only at those points. It proves continuity of a selected fixed-point family from a uniform local contraction and parameter continuity at the fixed base vector.

The original endpoint cutoff implies norm(q)<=n/16. The ACTUAL physical diagonal is bounded by2norm(q) on the WHOLE corrected strip. Its fixed-point map preserves the complete disk centered pi^2*n^2 of radius2norm(q),strictly inside the strip. Banach contraction constructs an ACTUAL scalar diagonal root with no root supplied by the caller.

endpointHillDiagonalRoot is the intrinsic actual root on the cutoff region. The ACTUAL equation,strict strip interior,quantitative original diagonal error and uniqueness on the ENTIRE corrected strip are proved. The total definition has a fallback outside the cutoff region;no root property is asserted there.

Under the strict cutoff criterion,the actual root is norm continuous. Its spectral diagonal derivative has norm<=1/8,so the derivative of lambda-free_n-a_n is nonzero. The checked analytic implicit-function theorem then proves COMPLEX analyticity of the actual root in the full endpoint potential,without an assumed branch or continuity hypothesis.

The article adapter retains original distributions and EXACT original endpoint norms. It proves the literal source equation,whole-strip uniqueness,mean-coefficient error,complex analyticity and real analyticity by scalar restriction. The same actual root is analytic on every stronger original source-weight space.

One cutoff BEFORE the original norm-ball potentials gives analytic root families with error2*C_r*n^(r-1/2)*R^2 relative to free_n+q0,and mean-zero displacement<=R/8. With R=2m this is exactly the source Lemma2.17 form8*C_r*n^(r-1/2)*m^2 and displacement<=m/4. Whole-strip uniqueness is retained. One cutoff also works BEFORE BOTH weight and potential in every original weighted norm ball.

sourceAdaptedCouplings defines the ACTUAL physical b_plus/minus evaluated at the proved intrinsic root. These coefficients are analytic in the EXACT original weighted norm,retain the full general-weight error bound,and have one uniform cutoff BEFORE BOTH weight and potential with shrinking error2*C_r*n^(r-1/2)*R^2.

At the proved actual diagonal root,the ORIGINAL physical effective determinant is exactly minus the product of the two actual adapted coefficients. The auxiliary diagonal root is not asserted to be a spectral eigenvalue or a spectral midpoint. The full adapted Fourier map Omega and its analytic inverse are not yet constructed.

domains.potentials: Full original complex period-two FourierLebesgueSpace(2,-r,infinity),0<=r<1/2. All original mean-zero physically period-one source potentials are included without changing the distribution.
domains.spectral_weights: All source SpectralWeight values are retained in the stronger weighted original-distribution restriction and adapted-coefficient errors.
domains.equation: alpha-pi^2*n^2-a_n(alpha,q)=0 for the literal physical diagonal a_n. The actual full H1/H-minus-one effective entries and original mean coefficient q0 are retained.
domains.cutoff: Native criterion C_r*n^(r-1/2)*norm(q)<=1/2 constructs the root and gives uniqueness on the ENTIRE corrected radius6n strip. Strict inequality gives analyticity. Every source norm-ball factory has a strict margin.
domains.source_cutoff: For original radius R,choose N with C_r*n^(r-1/2)*(8R)<=1/2 for every n>=N. Then C_r*n^(r-1/2)*norm(q)<=1/16 on the ball,including its boundary. This gives actual analytic extensions near every point of the source closed ball.
domains.uniformity: N is chosen BEFORE q;the weighted source factory chooses the SAME N BEFORE BOTH w and q.
domains.normalization: Original period-two exp(i*pi*k*x),free value pi^2*n^2,corrected strip radius6n and physical endpoint norm. No frequency or norm substitution.
domains.auxiliary_root: The root is an auxiliary diagonal root,not assumed/asserted to be an eigenvalue or spectral midpoint.

constants.fixed_point: Disk(center pi^2*n^2,radius2norm(q));contraction1/8;norm(q)<=n/16 keeps it strictly in the corrected strip.
constants.lemma_2_17: With R=2m,mean-zero displacement<=8*C_r*n^(r-1/2)*m^2 and<=m/4. Stronger statement accepts every real m,so includes the source m>=1 range.

qualifications: The actual root is CONSTRUCTED;no root table,continuity,analytic branch or simplicity is supplied as a caller assumption. The spectral derivative1-a_lambda is nonzero by the proved1/8 bound.

The total definition has a fallback outside the verified cutoff. Root properties are stated only under the cutoff;analyticity is stated under strict smallness. Source norm-ball cutoffs provide that strict margin.

Real analyticity over real scalars of a map to complex numbers is proved. Real-valuedness of alpha for real physical q,and conjugation/real-type preservation for the future Omega map,remain separate unproved dependencies.

The adapted-coefficient errors use the proved endpoint power n^(r-1/2);the source sharper log(n)/n^(1-r) refinement is not claimed here. These errors tend to0 and provide the needed near-identity construction inputs.
The full adapted Fourier map Omega,its Banach-valued analyticity,derivative/image-coverage/inverse estimates and source constraint preservation are NOT yet proved.
Source Theorem2.1(i) remains complete;Dirichlet Theorem2.1(ii),inverse Theorem2.2 and all MAIN theorems remain unproved.
remaining: Construct the ACTUAL adapted Fourier-coordinate map Omega^(m) from the now-proved analytic diagonal root and actual adapted couplings. Prove the physical conjugation/real-type symmetry that makes alpha_n(q) real and the adapted Fourier map real on real physical potentials. AnalyticAt over real scalars proved here is analyticity of a map to complex numbers;it does not by itself prove this real-valuedness.
